messages:
pavel: Holding the rollout for release r1.4.2 — canary is showing a perf regression on KV-heavy traces, p99 latency +18-25% on long-context tests. Pausing until we bisect.
anjali: saw the same in CI bench runs this morning, flagged it in the perf-dashboard.
tyler: rough summary from canary: throughput steady but tail latency spikes after ~6k tokens on repeated prefix workloads.
slo-bot: ALERT: route /generate (model: redwood-13b-q4) exceeded canary p95 SLO 3x in last 10m — automatic hold engaged.
kevin: initial hypothesis — the batching heuristic tweak (commit a7d9f3) plus the kernel-selector fallback logic might be causing early KV evictions. noticed more cache misses in the flamegraphs.
anjali: I profiled a canary instance and captured this snippet: 
```
kv_cache_hits: 0.73
kv_cache_misses: 0.27
avg_kv_entry_ttl: 42ms  # used to be ~120ms before the heuristic change
```
kevin: the new batch packing causes more fragmented key usage, combined with the kernel that prefers prefetched blocks; ends up thrashing the LRU windows.
samantha: can we reproduce deterministically with the replay harness? I can run a 10k-token replay set overnight.
tyler: yes, add the prefix-heavy test set (prefetch-heavy.json) — that matches user workload. Add env var `KV_EVICT_DEBUG=1` to gather evict traces.
pavel: good. while we repro, let's prepare a two-way bisect: revert batching heuristic commit a7d9f3, and separately revert kernel-selector change b3c0d1. aim: isolate which one dominates.
anjali: note: CI perf gate already failed on Friday for a different model variant (smoke CI showed 6% p99 regress). Might be related but not identical.
slo-bot: NOTE: rollout paused at 1793456801 by canary-gate. Manual approval required to continue.
kevin: I started a targeted canary with only the batching-revert on a single pool — launching now: `./deploy canary --pool=k1 --override=commit:a7d9f3:revert`
samantha: running the replay against that canary — initial 1000-token run looks better (p99 down ~5%), continuing full run.
tyler: if the batching revert fixes it, we can ship a small patch and unpause. if not, we'll rollback kernel-selector.
pavel: disagree on rolling both back at once — prefer sequential so we know cause. Also we should add a temporary guard: if canary p95 > SLO for 5m, auto-revert the release.
kevin: agreed. ops question: can we implement that guard in the rollout engine quickly or just enforce manual hold?
anjali: rollout engine supports a rule set, we can add `slo_window=5m, metric=p95, threshold=target*1.2, action=rollback` — it's a config change, I can submit a patch to the rollout repo.
pavel: do it, but don't enable globally — scope it to this release tag. add a manual opt-in flag.
samantha: repro finished — batching-revert canary looks within baseline: p99 delta -3%. Looks like batching heuristic was the main offender.
tyler: great. once we merge the revert, run a canary with kernel-selector change still present to be safe.
kevin: created PR to revert a7d9f3 and added a rollout rule on the canary config. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rollouts/pull/412
anjali: CI perf run for the revert PR shows green on the benchmark suite (p99 within 1%).
slo-bot: ACTION: rollback rule applied to release r1.4.2 canary (slo_window=5m, threshold=1.2x p95).
pavel: plan: merge revert, hold 30m canary, if stable then continue gradual rollout. document postmortem short note and add an integration test for prefix-heavy KV cache behavior.
kevin: follow-ups: add an e2e replay test that asserts avg_kv_entry_ttl doesn't drop below 80ms for the prefetched workload.
samantha: I'll open an eval to capture regression traces and add the test to nightly.
tyler: also adding more telemetry: expose per-kernel KV hit rate in runtime traces so future regressions are easier to attribute.
pavel: thanks all. ping me if any of the canaries flip back up. I'll coordinate a formal rollback if we see another spike. :thumbsup:
